request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export tree" button that downloads `tree.csv`. The file has the header line `sheet,name,grade,due-total`, then this sheet's people in list order, then the people of the other sheets in the tree, sorted by sheet id. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

How it works:
- **`src/main/frontend/features/summary/ExportTree.tsx`** (new): the button (`data-testid="export-tree"`). When pressed, it re-reads the tree's list of sheets and every sheet in it from the store, waits until all of them are loaded, then writes the file with the existing `downloadCsv` helper.
- **Due-totals** are worked out the same way as the existing tree search, so each person's figure matches what their row shows, including `n/a`. That logic lives in `TreeSearch.tsx`; I shared it rather than copying it and added the person's grade to what it returns.
- **`summary.slot.tsx`**: the button is placed on the screen just after the tree search.

No server or stored-data changes were needed, because the existing tree endpoint already lists a tree's sheets.

Two things I added that the request didn't ask for:
- The button is disabled while an export is running.
- If the tree can't be read, it shows an error (`export-tree-error`); the spec doesn't test this.

Choices I made where the request was silent:
- The grade column is each person's current grade.
- The file follows the sheet's current state, not an as-of date that's set on screen.
